questions.scenario: A recruitment company trains a model to screen CVs using ten years of historical hiring decisions. Most of the people hired during that period were men.
questions.question: What is the most likely risk of this approach?

options.text: The model will reproduce the historical bias and favour male candidates.
options.why: Correct. A model learns the patterns in its training data, including unfair ones.

options.text: The model will be unable to read CVs in PDF format.
options.why: File format is unrelated to the fairness risk described.

options.text: The model will expose candidate data publicly.
options.why: Nothing in the scenario indicates a data exposure risk.

options.text: The model will favour female candidates to balance the data.
options.why: Models do not correct historical imbalance on their own.

questions.explanation: Skewed training data is the most common source of unfairness. The model learns and repeats the historical pattern.

questions.scenario: A lender removes the gender column from its training data. Testing shows that the model still approves loans for women less often than for men with the same financial profile.
questions.question: What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: The model is using other features that act as proxies for gender.
options.why: Correct. Fields such as first name or occupation can still carry the same signal.

options.text: The model has a context window that is too small.
options.why: Context windows apply to language models and do not explain this outcome.

options.text: The temperature setting is too high.
options.why: Temperature affects generative output randomness, not loan scoring bias.

options.text: Removing a column always increases bias.
options.why: Removing the column is not the cause. Proxy features are.

questions.explanation: Removing a sensitive attribute does not guarantee fairness, because other features can act as proxies. Outcomes must be measured for each group.

questions.question: Which TWO actions help ensure that an AI system meets the inclusiveness principle?

options.text: Testing a speech solution with speakers who have a range of regional accents
options.why: Correct. Testing with representative users finds groups the system fails to serve.

options.text: Encrypting the training data at rest
options.why: Encryption supports privacy and security, not inclusiveness.

options.text: Providing captions and text input options for users who are deaf or hard of hearing
options.why: Correct. This makes the system usable by people with different abilities.

options.text: Assigning a named owner to approve each model release
options.why: Assigning an owner supports accountability.

questions.explanation: Inclusiveness means designing and testing AI so that people of all abilities, languages and backgrounds can use it.

questions.question: A team wants to determine whether its model performs equally well for different age groups. What should the team do?

options.text: Measure accuracy and outcomes separately for each age group.
options.why: Correct. Disaggregated evaluation reveals differences that an overall score can hide.

options.text: Report only the overall accuracy of the model.
options.why: An overall score can hide poor results for a specific group.

options.text: Increase the size of the model.
options.why: A larger model does not by itself show or fix group differences.

options.text: Remove all age-related data from the test set.
options.why: Without age information the team cannot compare results by age group.

questions.explanation: Evaluating results for each group, known as disaggregated evaluation, is the way to detect unfair performance.

questions.scenario: A government service chatbot currently responds only in English. Many citizens prefer to use regional languages.
questions.question: Adding support for regional languages primarily addresses which responsible AI principle?

options.text: Transparency
options.why: Transparency concerns explaining how the system works.

options.text: Inclusiveness
options.why: Correct. The change allows more people to use the service.

options.text: Reliability and safety
options.why: The chatbot is not failing or causing harm; it is excluding people.

options.text: Accountability
options.why: Accountability concerns responsibility and oversight.

questions.explanation: Supporting more languages makes the system usable by more people, which is the goal of inclusiveness.
